- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.6) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices after strong bullish sentiment spikes — adjust downward by 1–2% of forecasted peak.
- Overshoot in early forecast horizon (1–3 days) when sentiment is high — apply a 0.5–1.0% downward correction.
- Mean-reversion bias in mid-horizon (5–15 days) — if forecast is above 1.5σ above recent mean, reduce by 0.3–0.7σ.
- Lagged sentiment effects: if sentiment peaks 2–3 days prior, forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.2–0.5σ.
- Avoid overreacting to recent price drops — if sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is falling, forecast should not drop below 1.5σ below recent low.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overconfidence — cap maximum deviation at 1.2σ from 30-day moving average.
